Chrome DevTools Extension

includes a Chrome DevTools Extension that provides a dedicated DevTools panel for inspecting pipeline execution directly within Chrome Developer Tools. The extension captures deterministic execution traces, controller decisions, lifecycle transitions, and error events during application execution.

When enabled, the extension appears as a panel inside Chrome DevTools. From this panel engineers can inspect recorded pipeline activity, view state diffs, analyze hot stage rankings, replay pipeline executions, export diagnostic traces, and generate AI-assisted debugging reports.

The extension does not alter pipeline behavior. It operates as a passive observer that consumes telemetry produced by the Vault Monitor during pipeline execution.

The extension reconstructs execution traces by listening to Insight events emitted by instances during pipeline execution. Each recorded event represents a stage execution boundary, a lifecycle transition, a conductor decision, a controller vote, or a runtime error signal occurring within the pipeline.

By aggregating these events into deterministic traces, the extension allows engineers to inspect pipeline behavior, analyze performance, and reproduce runtime conditions outside of the running application.

For a deeper explanation of how runtime events are captured and monitored, see Vault Monitor.

Installing the Extension

The Chrome DevTools Extension is available from the Chrome Web Store. Installation requires Google Chrome or any Chromium-based browser that supports Chrome extensions.

Install the Extension

Add the Chrome DevTools Extension to inspect pipeline execution, view state diffs, and generate AI-assisted debugging reports — directly inside Chrome DevTools.

Install from Chrome Web Store

  1. Open the Chrome DevTools Extension listing in the Chrome Web Store.
  2. Select Add to Chrome and confirm the installation when prompted.
  3. Open Chrome DevTools in any application running with development mode enabled.
  4. Locate the panel tab in the DevTools toolbar.

Once installed, the extension automatically detects applications running with development mode enabled. No additional configuration is required beyond enabling development mode in the application runtime.

Enabling the Extension

The Chrome DevTools Extension requires the runtime to be initialized with development mode enabled. When development mode is active, the Vault Monitor exposes a global runtime handle that the extension bridge uses to connect and begin receiving pipeline telemetry.

To enable the extension, configure the Vault runtime with devMode: true. 

{{`// app.config.ts
export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({
      devMode: true,
    })
  ]
};`}}
 
{{`Vault({
  devMode: true,
});`}}

When the extension connects, its bridge script automatically activates global insights on the Vault Monitor with full telemetry enabled. The bridge enables the following insight attributes:

  • wantsState — captures full state snapshots for each pipeline event.
  • wantsPayload — captures payload data passed through pipeline stages.
  • wantsCandidates — captures in-flight candidate values at each stage boundary.
  • wantsErrors — captures error objects emitted during pipeline execution.

These attributes are activated globally by the extension bridge and do not need to be configured manually. Individual insight configurations are not required when using the Chrome DevTools Extension — the bridge overrides per-cell settings to ensure complete telemetry capture across all active cells.

When to Use the Extension

The Chrome DevTools Extension is designed to help engineers inspect runtime behavior inside the pipeline. It is particularly useful when investigating complex execution flows, performance characteristics, or controller decision outcomes.

  • Investigating unexpected pipeline behavior.
  • Tracing lifecycle transitions across instances.
  • Identifying performance bottlenecks in pipeline stages.
  • Comparing state before and after pipeline execution.
  • Debugging controller and conductor voting outcomes.
  • Replaying recorded pipeline executions for analysis.
  • Ranking hot stages to locate execution pressure.
  • Generating AI-assisted diagnostic reports for issue tracking.

Because the pipeline is deterministic, identical inputs produce identical execution traces on every run. This means that a trace captured during one session can be reliably compared against traces from subsequent sessions — stage ordering, controller votes, and lifecycle transitions remain consistent. Engineers can reproduce and analyze pipeline behavior with confidence that observed differences reflect actual changes in application logic rather than runtime variability.

Dimensions

The extension is designed for the Chrome DevTools panel, which can vary in size depending on docking position and screen resolution. For best results, ensure the DevTools panel meets the following minimum dimensions:

  • Width: 768px — below this threshold the extension switches to a narrow layout where action bars, diff panels, and comparison tables stack vertically instead of side by side.
  • Height: 500px — ensures report content, diff views, and event tables are visible without clipping. Diff panels use a fixed 400px content height, and the remaining space accommodates the toolbar and navigation controls.

The narrow layout remains fully functional at smaller widths. All report views adapt to the available space by reorganizing their content into a single-column flow.

Reports

The Chrome DevTools Extension organizes pipeline telemetry into specialized report views. Each report presents a different perspective on the captured execution data — from high-level registry summaries to granular stage-by-stage trace analysis.

Vault Overview

The Vault Overview report displays runtime package versions, license details, and the complete registry for the inspected application. Each registry card summarizes the behaviors, controllers, and fluent APIs attached to a cell, along with live trace statistics including total traces executed, average duration, and error count.

This report is useful for verifying that the expected instances are registered, confirming license status, and identifying cells with elevated error rates or unusually long average execution times. Selecting a cell opens a detail panel showing the full list of registered behaviors and controllers for that pipeline.

Feature Cell Events

The Feature Cell Events report displays a real-time log of every pipeline event emitted by the inspected application. Events are organized into two tabs — all events and error events — and can be filtered by cell, event type, behavior key, or free-text search. Selecting any event row reveals its full detail including state snapshot, payload data, and error information.

This report is useful for observing pipeline activity as it happens, isolating error events across instances, and verifying that expected lifecycle transitions and controller decisions are occurring during application execution. Events can be exported as structured JSON for offline analysis.

Hot Stage Ranking

The Hot Stage Ranking report aggregates pipeline stage durations across all captured traces and ranks stages by total cumulative execution time. Stages can be viewed individually or grouped by name to reveal which pipeline stages consume the most processing time across the application. Results can be filtered by cell to scope the analysis to a single instance.

This report is useful for identifying systemic performance bottlenecks that may not be visible in individual trace inspections. By ranking stages across all traces, engineers can locate execution pressure points and prioritize optimization efforts on the stages that contribute the most to overall pipeline duration.

Hot Stage Ranking requires a Pro License.

Pipeline Replay

The Pipeline Replay report dispatches a previously recorded trace through a live pipeline. Engineers select a cell and trace, review the original resolved value and trace summary, then replay the value through the same dispatch method used in the original execution. After replay, the report compares the original and replayed traces side by side with timeline visualizations and event-by-event diffs.

This report is useful for verifying that a code change produces the expected pipeline outcome. By replaying a trace before and after a fix, engineers can confirm whether behavior improved, regressed, or remained unchanged. Previously saved debug dumps can be loaded to replay traces from earlier sessions.

Pipeline Replay requires a Pro License.

State Diff

The State Diff report compares before and after state snapshots across pipeline stages within a single trace. Engineers select a cell and trace, then step through snapshot pairs to see exactly how state transforms at each stage boundary. A state mutation graph highlights which stages produced mutations for each candidate pair.

This report is useful for identifying unintended state mutations, verifying that specific pipeline stages are transforming state as expected, and understanding the cumulative effect of stage-by-stage processing within a single pipeline execution. Both a side-by-side diff view and a structured table view are available.

State Diff requires a Pro License.

Trace Details

The Trace Detail report displays completed pipeline traces as horizontal timeline bars with summary statistics for total traces, average duration, and outcome counts including success, error, denied, aborted, and orphaned traces. Expanding a trace reveals tabbed detail views for the event table, stage waterfall, pipeline flow, and hot stage ranking for that individual execution.

This report is useful for understanding how pipeline executions distribute over time, identifying traces that ended in error or denial, and drilling into a specific trace to inspect stage-by-stage timing, controller voting outcomes, and event metadata. Trace data can be filtered by cell and exported as structured JSON.

Trace Details requires a Pro License.

Debug Tools

The debug tools provide utilities for inspecting, exporting, and managing the internal state of the extension itself. These tools help engineers troubleshoot unexpected behavior, capture snapshots for offline analysis, and verify that the extension is operating correctly within the current page context.

AI Assist

The AI Assist tool exports a structured debug dump and an AI-assisted analysis prompt. Engineers download both files and upload them to a preferred AI model — such as ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini — to receive a comprehensive pipeline performance report with bottleneck detection and architectural insights.

This tool is useful for generating automated analysis of pipeline behavior without manually inspecting individual traces. The exported debug dump contains raw pipeline events, statistics, and registry data that the AI model uses to produce a structured diagnostic report.

AI Assist requires a Pro License.

Extension Inspector

The Extension Inspector filters all recorded pipeline data to a single controller or behavior key. Engineers select a cell and extension key to view execution count, duration statistics (average, minimum, and maximum), and the percentage of total trace time consumed by that extension. A per-trace breakdown shows how the selected key performed across every recorded execution.

This tool is useful for answering targeted performance questions about a specific controller or behavior — identifying whether it is consistently slow, how its duration varies across traces, and how much of the overall pipeline time it consumes. A detail view provides pipeline flow and candidate snapshot inspection for the selected extension.

Extension Inspector requires a Pro License.

Load Dump

The Load Dump tool imports a previously exported debug dump JSON file and replays the events through the trace pipeline. After loading, all DevTools views are populated with the dump data, giving engineers full access to trace timeline, controller voting decisions, behavior metrics, pipeline flow visualization, and hot stage ranking analysis.

This tool is useful for offline analysis of pipeline executions captured in another environment. Engineers can share dump files across teams, load them into their own DevTools instance, and inspect the full execution history without needing access to the original application. Loading a dump replaces all current session data.

Load Dump requires a Pro License.

Trace Export

The Trace Export tool exports recorded pipeline events as a Chrome Trace Timeline JSON file. The exported file can be loaded into Perfetto, the Chrome DevTools Performance tab, or chrome://tracing to visualize pipeline execution as an interactive flame chart with stage-level timing spans.

This tool is useful for analyzing pipeline stage execution ordering, identifying stage-level bottlenecks, and visualizing trace fan-out across pipelines. Engineers can share trace files with teammates or load them into familiar profiling tools for deeper investigation of behavior and controller timing.

Trace Export requires a Pro License.

Troubleshooting

If the Chrome DevTools Extension is not displaying pipeline events, check the following common issues.

  • Development mode is not enabled. The extension requires the Vault runtime to be initialized with devMode: true. Without development mode, the Vault Monitor does not expose the global runtime handle that the extension bridge uses to connect. Verify that your Vault configuration includes devMode: true as described in the Enabling the Extension section.
  • The DevTools panel was opened after the application loaded. The extension bridge connects when the Vault instantiates. If the DevTools panel is opened after the application has already initialized, the bridge misses the connection window. Refresh the webpage to re-instantiate the Vault and establish the connection.
  • No active on the current page. The extension only captures events when a is active and processing pipeline interactions. Navigate to a route whose component injects a service to begin generating events.
